input.title: Maintenance planning
input.pitch: A shared planning tool for small maintenance teams, now with an offline mobile app so technicians keep plans without connectivity.

evidence.text: Two vendors already sell maintenance scheduling at about 40 dollars per technician per month.
The founding team is two engineers with a six-month runway.
Field technicians report losing connectivity in basements and machinery rooms, where most scheduling happens.

concurrence.note: The offline gap differentiates against the two priced vendors named in the evidence.

cout.note: An offline app raises the build cost above the plain planning tool within the same runway.

temps.note: Two engineers can ship a pilot, but the offline app lengthens the time to a sellable release.

defendabilite.note: Offline-first for machinery-room conditions is a wedge the named vendors do not show.

acquisition.note: The offline pain gives crews a concrete reason to switch, per the field-technician evidence.

established_facts: Two vendors sell maintenance scheduling around 40 dollars per technician per month.
Field technicians report losing connectivity where most scheduling happens.

provenance.semantic_note: Iteration-linked recompute in English: the same idea after a payload change scores differently because new evidence arrived; proves recompute per iteration.
